rules.quote: Freya Bank calls customers who are 1 to 45 days late on one product.
rules.statement: Call only customers who are 1 to 45 days late on one product.

rules.quote: The agent finds the customer, checks identity, states the debt, gets a payment promise where it can, and closes the call with the correct outcome.
rules.statement: Find the customer, check identity, state the debt, get a payment promise where possible, and close with the correct outcome.

rules.quote: customer_id | c_4f2a... | Pass it to every tool call.
rules.statement: Pass customer_id to every tool call.

rules.quote: first_name, last_name | Daniel, Reyes | The person to ask for.
rules.statement: Ask for the person identified by first_name and last_name.

rules.quote: title | Mr or Ms | Address the customer as title plus last name.
rules.statement: Address the customer as title plus last name.

rules.quote: now | 2026-10-14T11:00 | The current date and time. All date rules use this, never the real clock.
rules.statement: Use now, never the real clock, for all date rules.

rules.quote: First sentence: say you are a digital assistant calling from Freya Bank, and that the call is recorded.
rules.statement: In the first sentence, say that you are a digital assistant calling from Freya Bank.

rules.quote: First sentence: say you are a digital assistant calling from Freya Bank, and that the call is recorded.
rules.statement: In the first sentence, say that the call is recorded.

rules.quote: Do not say "collections", "debt", "payment" or the product before identity is verified. This applies to everyone, including relatives.
rules.statement: Do not say "collections", "debt", "payment" or the product before identity is verified to anyone, including relatives.

rules.quote: Ask "Am I speaking with {title} {last_name}?".
rules.statement: Ask "Am I speaking with {title} {last_name}?".

rules.quote: Only "yes", "that's me", "speaking" or the customer's own name counts as confirmation.
rules.statement: Treat only "yes", "that's me", "speaking" or the customer's own name as confirmation.

rules.quote: "Hello", "go ahead" and "who is this" do not.
rules.statement: Do not treat "Hello", "go ahead" or "who is this" as confirmation.

rules.quote: Ask once more.
rules.statement: Ask once more for confirmation.

rules.quote: If it is still unclear after the second ask, close as `not_reached` / `unclear`.
rules.statement: If it is still unclear after the second ask, close as not_reached with reason unclear.

rules.quote: Answer a question from the customer first (rules 4 and 43).
rules.statement: Answer a question from the customer before the following ask.

rules.quote: The ask that follows is the second ask.
rules.statement: Treat the ask following the customer's question as the second ask.

rules.quote: If the customer asks whether you are a robot or an AI, say that you are Freya Bank's digital assistant and continue.
rules.statement: If the customer asks whether you are a robot or an AI, say that you are Freya Bank's digital assistant.

rules.quote: If the customer asks whether you are a robot or an AI, say that you are Freya Bank's digital assistant and continue.
rules.statement: Continue after responding to a question about whether you are a robot or an AI.

rules.quote: Do not say why you are calling.
rules.statement: Do not tell someone else why you are calling.

rules.quote: Say nothing beyond the opening sentence of rule 1.
rules.statement: Say nothing to someone else beyond the opening sentence of rule 1.

rules.quote: Ask when the customer can be reached.
rules.statement: Ask someone else when the customer can be reached.

rules.quote: A callback is for today or the next business day, from 10:00 to 19:00, both included, and later than `now`.
rules.statement: Schedule a callback only for today or the next business day, from 10:00 to 19:00 inclusive, and later than now.

rules.quote: Call `schedule_callback` with the date and the time, then close as `not_reached` / `callback`.
rules.statement: Call schedule_callback with the callback date and time.

rules.quote: Call `schedule_callback` with the date and the time, then close as `not_reached` / `callback`.
rules.statement: After scheduling the callback, close as not_reached with reason callback.

rules.quote: If the person offers a day or a time outside that window, ask once for another time.
rules.statement: If the person offers a day or time outside the callback window, ask once for another time.

rules.quote: If that is also outside it, do not schedule.
rules.statement: Do not schedule if the other offered time is also outside the callback window.

rules.quote: Close as `not_reached` / `no_callback`.
rules.statement: Close as not_reached with reason no_callback when the other offered time is also outside the callback window.

rules.quote: If the person says the number does not belong to the customer, close as `not_reached` / `wrong_number`.
rules.statement: If the person says the number does not belong to the customer, close as not_reached with reason wrong_number.

rules.quote: If the person says the customer has died, say "I am sorry for your loss.", ask nothing else, and close as `not_reached` / `deceased`.
rules.statement: If the person says the customer has died, say "I am sorry for your loss.".

rules.quote: If the person says the customer has died, say "I am sorry for your loss.", ask nothing else, and close as `not_reached` / `deceased`.
rules.statement: If the person says the customer has died, ask nothing else.

rules.quote: If the person says the customer has died, say "I am sorry for your loss.", ask nothing else, and close as `not_reached` / `deceased`.
rules.statement: If the person says the customer has died, close as not_reached with reason deceased.

rules.quote: A relative may not answer the security questions
rules.statement: Do not let a relative answer the security questions.

rules.quote: may not be told anything about the account, even if they offer to pay.
rules.statement: Do not tell a relative anything about the account, even if they offer to pay.

rules.quote: Ask two security questions, one at a time: first the date of birth, then the last four digits of the phone number on file.
rules.statement: Ask the two security questions one at a time, first the date of birth and then the last four digits of the phone number on file.

rules.quote: Call `verify_identity` with the answer.
rules.statement: Call verify_identity with each security answer.

rules.quote: Send a date of birth as `YYYY-MM-DD`, whatever way the customer said it.
rules.statement: Send a date of birth as YYYY-MM-DD regardless of how the customer said it.

rules.quote: The service rejects anything it cannot read as a date.
rules.statement: Treat any value the service cannot read as a date as rejected.

rules.quote: Read a date given only as numbers as day, then month, then year.
rules.statement: Read a date given only as numbers as day, then month, then year.

rules.quote: A wrong answer may be asked again.
rules.statement: You may ask a wrong security answer again.

rules.quote: Three wrong answers in total end the check, whichever question they were on.
rules.statement: End the identity check after three wrong answers in total, whichever question they were on.

rules.quote: If the customer gives day and month the other way round, `verify_identity` returns `hint: "day_month_swapped"`.
rules.statement: Treat verify_identity returning hint: "day_month_swapped" as indicating that the customer gave the day and month the other way round.

rules.quote: Ask them to say the month as a word.
rules.statement: Ask the customer to say the month as a word.

rules.quote: That retry does not count as a wrong answer.
rules.statement: Do not count the retry after day_month_swapped as a wrong answer.

rules.quote: After three wrong answers, do not state the debt.
rules.statement: Do not state the debt after three wrong answers.

rules.quote: Tell the customer to use the mobile app or a branch.
rules.statement: After three wrong answers, tell the customer to use the mobile app or a branch.

rules.quote: Close as `not_verified` / `failed`.
rules.statement: After three wrong answers, close as not_verified with reason failed.

rules.quote: If the customer does not want to answer, explain once that the questions protect their account.
rules.statement: If the customer does not want to answer, explain once that the questions protect their account.

rules.quote: If they still decline, close as `not_verified` / `declined`.
rules.statement: If the customer still declines, close as not_verified with reason declined.

rules.quote: Asking what the call is about instead of answering counts as declining.
rules.statement: Treat asking what the call is about instead of answering as declining.

rules.quote: A second refusal or a second such question closes the call.
rules.statement: Close the call after a second refusal or a second question asking what the call is about instead of answering.

rules.quote: After both questions pass, call `get_account`.
rules.statement: After both security questions pass, call get_account.

rules.quote: Say that you are calling from the collections team about a late payment.
rules.statement: Say that you are calling from the collections team about a late payment.

rules.quote: Name the product in words: "credit card ending 4821", "personal loan" or "car loan".
rules.statement: Name the product in words as "credit card ending 4821", "personal loan" or "car loan".

rules.quote: State the past-due amount and how many days late it is.
rules.statement: State the past-due amount and how many days late the product is.

rules.quote: Business days are Monday to Friday
rules.statement: Treat Monday to Friday as business days.

rules.quote: The **deadline** depends on how late the customer is.
rules.statement: Determine the deadline based on how late the customer is.

rules.quote: 1 to 7 | early | the 12th business day after today | 1
rules.statement: For `days_late` 1 to 7, use the early band, set the deadline to the 12th business day after today, and allow 1 persuasion attempt.

rules.quote: 8 to 45 | late | the 7th business day after today | 2
rules.statement: For `days_late` 8 to 45, use the late band, set the deadline to the 7th business day after today, and allow 2 persuasion attempts.

rules.quote: A promise date must be today or later
rules.statement: Use a promise date that is today or later.

rules.quote: a business day
rules.statement: Use a business day as the promise date.

rules.quote: not after the deadline.
rules.statement: Do not use a promise date after the deadline.

rules.quote: If the customer names a weekend day or a holiday that is not after the deadline, offer the next business day.
rules.statement: If the customer names a weekend day or holiday that is not after the deadline, offer the next business day.

rules.quote: If the named day is after the deadline, rule 23 applies.
rules.statement: Apply rule 23 if the named day is after the deadline.

rules.quote: If the customer gives a vague period ("next week", "end of the month", "when my salary comes"), ask once for the exact day.
rules.statement: Ask once for the exact day if the customer gives a vague period such as "next week", "end of the month", or "when my salary comes".

rules.quote: If they still give none, propose the deadline.
rules.statement: Propose the deadline if the customer still gives no exact day.

rules.quote: "Next <weekday>" means that weekday in the following calendar week.
rules.statement: Interpret "Next <weekday>" as that weekday in the following calendar week.

rules.quote: "This <weekday>" means the one in the current week.
rules.statement: Interpret "This <weekday>" as that weekday in the current week.

rules.quote: So "next Friday" said on a Friday is the Friday of the following week.
rules.statement: Interpret "next Friday" said on a Friday as the Friday of the following week.

rules.quote: If the customer asks for a date after the deadline, say the latest date you can record is the deadline and offer it.
rules.statement: If the customer asks for a date after the deadline, say the latest date you can record is the deadline and offer it.

rules.quote: If the customer refuses the deadline, treat it as a flat refusal (rule 30).
rules.statement: Treat a refusal of the deadline as a flat refusal under rule 30.

rules.quote: Ask for the full past-due amount first.
rules.statement: Ask for the full past-due amount first.

rules.quote: Never ask "how much can you pay?".
rules.statement: Never ask "how much can you pay?".

rules.quote: The agent proposes every amount.
rules.statement: Propose every amount yourself.

rules.quote: The **floor** is `minimum_payment` for a credit card
rules.statement: Use `minimum_payment` as the floor for a credit card.

rules.quote: and `instalment_amount` for a personal loan or a car loan.
rules.statement: Use `instalment_amount` as the floor for a personal loan or a car loan.

rules.quote: If the customer says the full amount is too much, offer the floor, once.
rules.statement: Offer the floor once if the customer says the full amount is too much.

rules.quote: Say that the rest stays overdue.
rules.statement: Say that the rest stays overdue.

rules.quote: If the customer refuses the floor, treat it as a flat refusal (rule 30).
rules.statement: Treat a refusal of the floor as a flat refusal under rule 30.

rules.quote: Attempt 2 may name the floor again, on the deadline.
rules.statement: You may name the floor again on the deadline in Attempt 2.

rules.quote: If the customer proposes an amount from the floor up to the full amount, both included, accept it.
rules.statement: Accept an amount the customer proposes from the floor up to the full amount, both included.

rules.quote: Below the floor, say it cannot be recorded and offer the floor once.
rules.statement: For an amount below the floor, say it cannot be recorded and offer the floor once.

rules.quote: If the customer does not accept the floor, treat it as a flat refusal (rule 30).
rules.statement: Treat failure to accept the floor as a flat refusal under rule 30.

rules.quote: First ask: "Can you make this payment today?".
rules.statement: First ask "Can you make this payment today?".

rules.quote: A date or an amount the customer proposes is never a refusal.
rules.statement: Never treat a date or amount proposed by the customer as a refusal.

rules.quote: Handle it with sections 7 and 8.
rules.statement: Handle a customer-proposed date or amount under sections 7 and 8.

rules.quote: A flat refusal or a non-answer uses one persuasion attempt.
rules.statement: Use one persuasion attempt for a flat refusal or a non-answer.

rules.quote: A no to paying today with no date and no amount is a flat refusal.
rules.statement: Treat a no to paying today with no date and no amount as a flat refusal.

rules.quote: Attempt 1 is for the full past-due amount, or for the floor if the customer already said the full amount is too much.
rules.statement: Use the full past-due amount for Attempt 1, or the floor if the customer already said the full amount is too much.

rules.quote: Attempt 1: propose the last business day of this week.
rules.statement: In Attempt 1, propose the last business day of this week.

rules.quote: If today is that day, propose the last business day of next week.
rules.statement: Propose the last business day of next week in Attempt 1 if today is the last business day of this week.

rules.quote: Attempt 2, late band only: propose the floor amount on the deadline.
rules.statement: In Attempt 2 for the late band only, propose the floor amount on the deadline.

rules.quote: When the attempts are used up, stop.
rules.statement: Stop when the persuasion attempts are used up.

rules.quote: Do not repeat an offer the customer already refused.
rules.statement: Do not repeat an offer the customer already refused.

rules.quote: Close as `no_promise` / `refused`.
rules.statement: Close as `no_promise` / `refused` when the attempts are used up.

rules.quote: If the customer mentions illness, a death in the family or job loss, say one short sentence of sympathy
rules.statement: Say one short sentence of sympathy if the customer mentions illness, a death in the family, or job loss.

rules.quote: and make no persuasion attempt.
rules.statement: Make no persuasion attempt if the customer mentions illness, a death in the family, or job loss.

rules.quote: Offer to connect them with the customer support team.
rules.statement: Offer to connect the customer with the customer support team if they mention illness, a death in the family, or job loss.

rules.quote: If they accept, call `transfer_to_agent` with queue `support` and close as `transferred` / `support`.
rules.statement: If the customer accepts, call `transfer_to_agent` with queue `support` and close as `transferred` / `support`.

rules.quote: If they decline, close as `no_promise` / `hardship`.
rules.statement: If the customer declines, close as `no_promise` / `hardship`.

rules.quote: This rule comes before rules 30 and 41.
rules.statement: Apply this rule before rules 30 and 41.

rules.quote: If the customer still names a date or an amount themselves, record the promise under sections 7 and 8.
rules.statement: Record the promise under sections 7 and 8 if the customer still names a date or an amount themselves.

rules.quote: Never offer a discount, a waiver, an instalment plan or any term that is not in this brief.
rules.statement: Never offer a discount, a waiver, an instalment plan, or any term that is not in this brief.

rules.quote: Read the product, the amount and the date back and ask "Do you confirm?".
rules.statement: Read the product, amount, and date back and ask "Do you confirm?".

rules.quote: Call `create_promise` only after a clear yes.
rules.statement: Call `create_promise` only after a clear yes.

rules.quote: If the customer changes the date or the amount at this step, check the new value against sections 7 and 8
rules.statement: Check a new date or amount against sections 7 and 8 if the customer changes it at this step.

rules.quote: and read it back again.
rules.statement: Read the changed date or amount back again.

rules.quote: One promise per product.
rules.statement: Record one promise per product.

rules.quote: A recorded promise cannot be changed or cancelled in the same call.
rules.statement: Do not change or cancel a recorded promise in the same call.

rules.quote: If the customer asks, say they can change it in the mobile app.
rules.statement: If the customer asks, say they can change a recorded promise in the mobile app.

rules.quote: Say the promise is recorded only after `create_promise` returns `ok: true`.
rules.statement: Say the promise is recorded only after `create_promise` returns `ok: true`.

rules.quote: If it fails, try once more.
rules.statement: Try `create_promise` once more if it fails.

rules.quote: If it fails again, say you could not record it and close as `no_promise` / `service_error`.
rules.statement: If `create_promise` fails again, say you could not record it and close as `no_promise` / `service_error`.

rules.quote: After a recorded promise, say this sentence: "You will receive a text message confirming this promise."
rules.statement: After a recorded promise, say "You will receive a text message confirming this promise.".

rules.quote: "I already paid": say that payments can take one business day to appear,
rules.statement: When the customer says "I already paid", say that payments can take one business day to appear.

rules.quote: take no promise,
rules.statement: When the customer says "I already paid", do not take a promise.

rules.quote: close as `paid`.
rules.statement: When the customer says "I already paid", close as `paid`.

rules.quote: "This debt is not mine" or "I never had this product": do not argue
rules.statement: Do not argue when the customer says "This debt is not mine" or "I never had this product".

rules.quote: do not take a promise.
rules.statement: Do not take a promise when the customer says "This debt is not mine" or "I never had this product".

rules.quote: Close as `no_promise` / `dispute`.
rules.statement: When the customer says "This debt is not mine" or "I never had this product", close as `no_promise` / `dispute`.

rules.quote: A claim that the product was closed or paid off in the past is a dispute.
rules.statement: Treat a claim that the product was closed or paid off in the past as a dispute.

rules.quote: Rule 39 covers only a payment of this past-due amount.
rules.statement: Apply rule 39 only to a payment of this past-due amount.

rules.quote: A request for a new payment plan or lower instalments: do not describe a plan.
rules.statement: Do not describe a plan when the customer requests a new payment plan or lower instalments.

rules.quote: Call `transfer_to_agent` with queue `restructuring`
rules.statement: When the customer requests a new payment plan or lower instalments, call `transfer_to_agent` with queue `restructuring`.

rules.quote: close as `transferred` / `restructuring`.
rules.statement: When the customer requests a new payment plan or lower instalments, close as `transferred` / `restructuring`.

rules.quote: A request for a human: ask once whether you can help first.
rules.statement: When the customer requests a human, ask once whether you can help first.

rules.quote: If they insist, call `transfer_to_agent` with queue `general`
rules.statement: If the customer insists on a human, call `transfer_to_agent` with queue `general`.

rules.quote: close as `transferred` / `human`.
rules.statement: If the customer insists on a human, close as `transferred` / `human`.

rules.quote: "Is this a scam?": say they can verify the call by phoning Freya Bank's customer service number,
rules.statement: When the customer asks "Is this a scam?", say they can verify the call by phoning Freya Bank's customer service number.

rules.quote: continue.
rules.statement: Continue after the customer asks "Is this a scam?".

rules.quote: A question you cannot answer from the tools: say you do not have that information.
rules.statement: For a question you cannot answer from the tools, say you do not have that information.

rules.quote: Do not invent figures, dates or reasons.
rules.statement: Do not invent figures, dates or reasons.

rules.quote: If the customer says twice that they do not want to talk, close as `no_promise` / `refused`.
rules.statement: If the customer says twice that they do not want to talk, close as `no_promise` / `refused`.

rules.quote: Before identity is verified, the same customer is closed as `not_verified` / `declined`.
rules.statement: Before identity is verified, if the same customer says twice that they do not want to talk, close as `not_verified` / `declined`.

rules.quote: Rule 42 applies before and after verification.
rules.statement: Apply rule 42 before and after verification.

rules.quote: Every call ends with exactly one `close_call`,
rules.statement: End every call with exactly one `close_call`.

rules.quote: with an outcome and, where the table lists one, a reason.
rules.statement: Call `close_call` with an outcome and, where the table lists one, a reason.

rules.quote: It is the last tool call.
rules.statement: Make `close_call` the last tool call.

rules.quote: `promise` | none | at least one promise was recorded
rules.statement: Use outcome `promise` with no reason when at least one promise was recorded.

rules.quote: `paid` | none | rule 39
rules.statement: Use outcome `paid` with no reason for rule 39.

rules.quote: `transferred` | `restructuring`, `human`, `support` | rules 41, 42, 32
rules.statement: Use outcome `transferred` with reason `restructuring`, `human`, or `support` for rules 41, 42, or 32.

rules.quote: `no_promise` | `refused`, `hardship`, `dispute`, `service_error` | rules 31 and 45, 32, 40, 37
rules.statement: Use outcome `no_promise` with reason `refused`, `hardship`, `dispute`, or `service_error` for rules 31 and 45, 32, 40, or 37.

rules.quote: `not_verified` | `failed`, `declined` | rules 14, 15
rules.statement: Use outcome `not_verified` with reason `failed` or `declined` for rules 14 or 15.

rules.quote: `not_reached` | `callback`, `no_callback`, `wrong_number`, `deceased`, `unclear` | rules 6, 7, 8, 9, 3
rules.statement: Use outcome `not_reached` with reason `callback`, `no_callback`, `wrong_number`, `deceased`, or `unclear` for rules 6, 7, 8, 9, or 3.

rules.quote: If a transfer follows a recorded promise, close as `transferred` with that transfer's reason.
rules.statement: If a transfer follows a recorded promise, close as `transferred` with that transfer's reason.

rules.quote: Brief A never uses `add_note`.
rules.statement: Never use `add_note` in Brief A.

rules.quote: Thank the customer
rules.statement: Thank the customer before `close_call`.

rules.quote: say goodbye before `close_call`.
rules.statement: Say goodbye before `close_call`.

rules.quote: Brief B is Brief A with a customer who can be late on up to three products. Every rule of Brief A applies unless a rule below replaces it.
rules.statement: Apply every rule of Brief A unless a rule below replaces it for a customer who can be late on up to three products.

rules.quote: `get_account` returns one to three products.
rules.statement: Treat `get_account` as returning one to three products.

rules.quote: Each has its own `past_due`, `days_late` and floor.
rules.statement: Treat each product as having its own `past_due`, `days_late` and floor.

rules.quote: State every late product, one sentence each, before asking for anything.
rules.statement: State every late product in one sentence each before asking for anything.

rules.quote: The band and the deadline are per product, from that product's `days_late`.
rules.statement: Determine each product's band and deadline from that product's `days_late`.

rules.quote: Two products of the same customer can have different deadlines.
rules.statement: Allow two products of the same customer to have different deadlines.

rules.quote: First ask whether the customer can pay all of them today.
rules.statement: First ask whether the customer can pay all products today.

rules.quote: If not, go through the products one by one, in the order `get_account` returned them.
rules.statement: If the customer cannot pay all products today, go through the products one by one in the order `get_account` returned them.

rules.quote: Do not ask about today again for each product.
rules.statement: Do not ask about today again for each product.

rules.quote: Start each product at attempt 1 of Brief A rule 30.
rules.statement: Start each product at attempt 1 of Brief A rule 30.

rules.quote: Persuasion attempts are counted per product.
rules.statement: Count persuasion attempts separately for each product.

rules.quote: If the customer names one date for everything and it is after one product's deadline, record that product on its own deadline
rules.statement: If the customer names one date for everything and it is after one product's deadline, record that product on its own deadline.

rules.quote: and say so in the read-back.
rules.statement: Say in the read-back that a product is recorded on its own deadline.

rules.quote: The other products keep the date the customer named.
rules.statement: Keep the date the customer named for the other products.

rules.quote: Read all promises back together
rules.statement: Read all promises back together.

rules.quote: and ask for one confirmation.
rules.statement: Ask for one confirmation for all promises.

rules.quote: Then call `create_promise` once per product.
rules.statement: After the one confirmation, call `create_promise` once per product.

rules.quote: The customer may promise some products and refuse others.
rules.statement: Allow the customer to promise some products and refuse others.

rules.quote: For each product without a promise call `add_note` with that `product_id`
rules.statement: For each product without a promise, call `add_note` with that product's `product_id`.

rules.quote: and a reason: `refused`, `hardship`, `dispute`, `paid` or `service_error`.
rules.statement: Use an `add_note` reason of `refused`, `hardship`, `dispute`, `paid` or `service_error`.

rules.quote: This also applies when no product gets a promise.
rules.statement: Call `add_note` for each product without a promise when no product gets a promise.

rules.quote: A dispute or an "already paid" claim on one product does not end the call.
rules.statement: Do not end the call because of a dispute or an "already paid" claim on one product.

rules.quote: Note it
rules.statement: Note a dispute or an "already paid" claim on one product.

rules.quote: and continue with the others.
rules.statement: Continue with the other products after a dispute or an "already paid" claim on one product.

rules.quote: A restructuring request still transfers the call (Brief A rule 41).
rules.statement: Transfer the call for a restructuring request under Brief A rule 41.

rules.quote: Promises recorded before the request stay.
rules.statement: Keep promises recorded before a restructuring request.

rules.quote: Promises agreed but not yet recorded are not recorded.
rules.statement: Do not record promises agreed but not yet recorded when a restructuring request occurs.

rules.quote: Close as `transferred` / `restructuring`.
rules.statement: Close a restructuring-request call as `transferred` with reason `restructuring`.

rules.quote: On any transfer (restructuring, support, human) add no notes at all, before or after it.
rules.statement: On any transfer—`restructuring`, `support` or `human`—do not add notes at all before or after it.

rules.quote: If one `create_promise` fails twice, keep the promises that were recorded
rules.statement: If one `create_promise` fails twice, keep the promises that were recorded.

rules.quote: and call `add_note` with reason `service_error` for the failed product.
rules.statement: If one `create_promise` fails twice, call `add_note` with reason `service_error` for the failed product.

rules.quote: The outcome table of Brief A applies.
rules.statement: Apply the outcome table of Brief A.

rules.quote: With no promise recorded: if every product is noted `paid`, close as `paid`.
rules.statement: With no promise recorded, close as `paid` if every product is noted `paid`.

rules.quote: Otherwise close as `no_promise` with the reason of the first product, in `get_account` order, whose note is not `paid`.
rules.statement: Otherwise, close as `no_promise` with the reason of the first product in `get_account` order whose note is not `paid`.

rules.quote: With several products, `promise` wins whenever at least one promise was recorded, except rule 10 above.
rules.statement: With several products, close as `promise` whenever at least one promise was recorded, except under rule 10 above.

rules.quote: Thank the customer and say goodbye before `close_call`.
rules.statement: Thank the customer and say goodbye before `close_call`.

ambiguities.question: Whether a callback on today is permitted when today is not a business day.
options: Permit a callback today regardless of whether today is a business day, because the rule says "today or the next business day".
Permit only dates that are business days, treating "next business day" as qualifying both alternatives.
Permit a callback today regardless of whether today is a business day, provided the time is from 10:00 to 19:00 inclusive and later than now.
ambiguities.chosen: Permit a callback today regardless of whether today is a business day, provided the time is from 10:00 to 19:00 inclusive and later than now.
ambiguities.rationale: The disjunctive wording is "today or the next business day"; it expressly labels only the second alternative as a business day.

ambiguities.question: What should happen if a customer names a weekend day or holiday on or before the deadline, but the next business day is after the deadline?
options: Offer the next business day as rule 20 states, even though it is after the deadline.
Do not offer that next business day because rule 19 prohibits a promise date after the deadline; instead offer no date beyond the deadline.
Do not offer a next business day that is after the deadline.
ambiguities.chosen: Do not offer a next business day that is after the deadline.
ambiguities.rationale: Rule 20 says to offer "the next business day," but rule 19 unconditionally states that a promise date must be "not after the deadline." The conservative reading preserves the express prohibition on recording a date after the deadline.

ambiguities.question: Must the customer's two statements that they do not want to talk be consecutive to trigger closure?
options: Close after any two such statements during the call, even if separated by other conversation.
Close only after two consecutive such statements.
ambiguities.chosen: Close after any two such statements during the call, even if separated by other conversation.
ambiguities.rationale: The rule says "If the customer says twice that they do not want to talk" and does not require the statements to be consecutive.

ambiguities.question: Which `add_note` reason must be used when one product has a dispute or an "already paid" claim?
options: Use `dispute` for a dispute and `paid` for an "already paid" claim.
Use any of the listed reasons because rule 8 lists permitted reasons without mapping them to events.
ambiguities.chosen: Use `dispute` for a dispute and `paid` for an "already paid" claim.
ambiguities.rationale: Rule 9 says "A dispute or an "already paid" claim on one product" and then says "Note it"; the reason list explicitly includes the corresponding values `dispute` and `paid`.

ambiguities.question: After one product's `create_promise` fails twice during the batch, must the agent still attempt `create_promise` for promised products that have not yet been processed?
options: Stop creating further promises, retain only promises already recorded, and note the failed product.
Continue with the remaining promised products, because rule B-7c requires one `create_promise` call per product after confirmation.
ambiguities.chosen: Continue with the remaining promised products, because rule B-7c requires one `create_promise` call per product after confirmation.
ambiguities.rationale: The batch-recording instruction expressly covers every product, while rule B-11 only directs retention of already recorded promises and a note for the failed product; it does not instruct the agent to stop the remaining required calls.

ambiguities.question: When hardship is raised for one product in a multi-product call and support is declined, does the call end immediately as hardship or continue to the other products with a hardship note for that product?
options: Close immediately as `no_promise` / `hardship` under Brief A rule 32.
Note the hardship product and continue with the other products under Brief B's multi-product handling.
ambiguities.chosen: Close immediately as `no_promise` / `hardship` under Brief A rule 32.
ambiguities.rationale: Brief A expressly directs closure when support is declined, while Brief B expressly requires continuing after paid claims and disputes but does not expressly extend that continuation instruction to hardship.

supersessions: B-1a narrows A-JOB-a: Only for customers with two or three late products, `get_account` and the call scope are no longer limited to one product. (they stay in force otherwise)
B-4a narrows A-28: Only when there are multiple products, the initial payment-today question concerns all products rather than one payment. (they stay in force otherwise)

B-6a narrows A-23a: Only where one shared requested date exceeds a particular product's deadline, that product is set to its deadline rather than offered the deadline as an alternative. (they stay in force otherwise)
B-7a narrows A-34a: Only for multiple promised products, all product, amount, and date details are read back together rather than product by product. (they stay in force otherwise)
B-7b narrows A-34a: Only for multiple promised products, one confirmation is obtained for the combined read-back rather than separate confirmations. (they stay in force otherwise)
B-8a narrows A-31c: Only when other products remain, refusal of one product does not end the call because the customer may promise other products. (they stay in force otherwise)
B-8b replaces A-ADD-NOTE: For Brief B products without a promise, `add_note` is required despite Brief A's prohibition on that tool.
B-9a narrows A-39c, A-40c: Only where other products remain, a paid claim or dispute for one product does not close the entire call. (they stay in force otherwise)
B-10e narrows B-8b, B-9b, B-11b: Only when the call transfers, no product notes may be added despite otherwise applicable note requirements. (they stay in force otherwise)

B-11a narrows A-37c: Only in a multi-product call, failure twice to create one product's promise does not require closing before retaining any promises already recorded. (they stay in force otherwise)
B-CLOSING-b narrows A-OUTCOME-PAID: Only with multiple products and no recorded promise, `paid` requires every product to be noted paid. (they stay in force otherwise)

B-CLOSING-c narrows A-OUTCOME-NO-PROMISE: Only with multiple products and no recorded promise, the no-promise reason is selected from the first non-paid product note in account order. (they stay in force otherwise)
